summary: When IPv6 datagrams using LoWPAN encapsulation (RFC 4944) travel over Layer 2 technologies such as Ethernet, the receiver must be able to recognize them. This informational document records the Ethertype that was assigned for that purpose.

plainLanguage.summary: When different kinds of packages travel on the same belt, each needs a label to say what is inside. This records the label number for the compressed small-device IPv6 packages.

questions: what ethertype is assigned for lowpan
how to identify lowpan encapsulated ipv6 on ethernet
subtitle: A protocol label for IPv6 with LoWPAN encapsulation over Ethernet

tldr.problem: IPv6 datagrams using LoWPAN encapsulation, a compression format for small devices, need a way to be identified when carried over Layer 2 technologies like Ethernet so receivers know how to interpret them.
tldr.mechanism: The IETF requested that IEEE assign an Ethertype (a Layer 2 protocol identifier) for LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6 datagrams. IEEE assigned Ethertype 0xA0ED (decimal 41197) for this purpose.
tldr.outcome: Network devices, protocol analyzers, and Layer 2 technologies can now recognize and properly handle LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6 traffic, enabling its use in new contexts like IEEE 802.15.9 multiplexing and Wi-Fi HaLoW.

today: RFC 7973 is an Informational RFC that remains current. The Ethertype assignment is now active in the IEEE 802 Numbers registry and can be used by any Layer 2 technology that needs to carry LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6 traffic.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content:
LoWPAN encapsulation, defined in RFC 4944, is a way to compress IPv6 datagrams for low-power wireless devices. When these compressed datagrams travel over Layer 2 technologies like Ethernet, which use protocol identifiers called Ethertypes, the receiving device needs to know that the payload is LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6.

Without an assigned Ethertype, debugging tools like Wireshark cannot recognize the format, and standards like IEEE 802.15.9 (which provides multiplexed data services) cannot dispatch these frames properly.
sections.plainLanguage: Small devices compress their data before sending it. When that compressed data comes over Ethernet cables, the receiving machine needs to know it is compressed.

sections.title: The Assignment
sections.content:
The IETF formally requested an Ethertype assignment from IEEE. IEEE assigned Ethertype 0xA0ED (which is 41197 in decimal) for this purpose. This value is now the official identifier for IPv6 datagrams using LoWPAN encapsulation when carried over Ethernet.

This assignment enables several use cases: Wi-Fi Alliance's HaLoW standard (low-power Wi-Fi in the 900 MHz band), Wi-SUN networks that use IEEE 802.15.9, and any other Layer 2 technology that needs to dispatch LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6 packets.
sections.plainLanguage: The official label number for compressed IPv6 on regular Ethernet is now 41197 in decimal or 0xA0ED in hexadecimal.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: This document only assigns a protocol identifier. It creates no new security issues. The security properties of LoWPAN encapsulation are defined by the encapsulation mechanism itself, and the security considerations of IPv6 still apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Just assigning a label does not make anything safer or more dangerous.
